title: Jeremiah Chapter 37 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 37 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 37 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 37.

questions.question: Who reigned as king instead of Coniah in the land of Judah?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:1 states that king Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim.

questions.question: Did king Zedekiah and his people listen to the words of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:2 clearly states that neither king Zedekiah, nor his servants, nor the people hearkened unto the words of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah.

questions.question: Whom did king Zedekiah send to the prophet Jeremiah to ask him to pray for them?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:3 states that Zedekiah sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah to pray for them.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was put into prison before he came in and went out among the people.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:4 says Jeremiah came in and went out among the people because they had not put him into prison.

questions.question: What caused the Chaldeans to depart from Jerusalem temporarily?
options: Pharaoh's army coming out of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh's army coming out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:5 explains that when Pharaoh's army came out of Egypt, the Chaldeans who besieged Jerusalem departed from the city.

questions.question: Who spoke to Jeremiah after the Chaldeans departed from Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:6 says the word of the LORD came to the prophet Jeremiah after the Chaldeans left.

questions.question: What did the LORD say about Pharaoh's army that came to help Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:7 states that the LORD said Pharaoh's army which came to help will return to Egypt into their own land.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promised Jerusalem peace from the Chaldeans after Pharaoh's army arrived.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:8 and 37:9 reveal the LORD said the Chaldeans would come again, fight, take the city, and burn it; they will not depart.

questions.question: What did the LORD say would happen even if the Chaldean army was smitten and only wounded men remained?
options: They would rise up and burn the city
questions.correctAnswer: They would rise up and burn the city
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:10 states that even if the Chaldean army was smitten, the wounded men would rise up and burn Jerusalem with fire.

questions.question: Which event happened first according to Jeremiah 37:11-13?
options: Jeremiah went into the land of Benjamin
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:11 states the Chaldeans broke up from Jerusalem first, then Jeremiah went to Benjamin (verse 12) and was taken by Irijah (verse 13).

questions.question: Who accused Jeremiah of falling away to the Chaldeans?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:13 introduces Irijah, the captain of the ward, accusing Jeremiah of falling away to the Chaldeans.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah admitted to falling away to the Chaldeans when accused.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:14 records Jeremiah denying the accusation, saying, 'It is false; I fall not away to the Chaldeans.'

questions.question: What did the princes do to Jeremiah after he was brought before them?
options: They smote him and put him in prison
questions.correctAnswer: They smote him and put him in prison
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:15 tells that the princes were wroth with Jeremiah, smote him, and put him in prison.

questions.question: Where was Jeremiah imprisoned by the princes?
options: In the house of Jonathan the scribe
In the court of the prison
questions.correctAnswer: In the house of Jonathan the scribe
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:15 states the princes put Jeremiah in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe, which they had made into a prison.

questions.question: After many days in the dungeon, what did King Zedekiah do with Jeremiah?
options: He sent and took him out to ask secretly about the word of the LORD
He ordered him to be executed
questions.correctAnswer: He sent and took him out to ask secretly about the word of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:17 says Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah, took him out secretly, and asked if there was any word from the LORD.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 37 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 37 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who reigned as king of Judah instead of Coniah according to Jeremiah 37?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:1 states that king Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadrezzar made king.

questions.question: What was the response of King Zedekiah, his servants, and the people to the words of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:2 says that neither Zedekiah, his servants, nor the people hearkened unto the words of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah.

questions.question: Whom did King Zedekiah send to the prophet Jeremiah to pray for the people?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:3 records that Zedekiah sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah to pray for them.

questions.question: Why was Jeremiah able to come and go freely among the people at this time?
options: Because he was released from prison
Because they had not put him into prison
questions.correctAnswer: Because they had not put him into prison
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:4 states Jeremiah came in and went out among the people because they had not put him into prison.

questions.question: What caused the Chaldeans to depart from Jerusalem temporarily?
options: The arrival of Pharaoh's army from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The arrival of Pharaoh's army from Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:5 explains that when Pharaoh's army came forth from Egypt, the Chaldeans who besieged Jerusalem departed from the city.

questions.question: What did the LORD say would happen to Pharaoh's army that came to help Judah?
options: They would join forces with Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:7 records the LORD's word that Pharaoh's army would return to Egypt into their own land.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 37, what will happen after the Chaldeans return to fight Jerusalem again?
options: The city will be taken and burned with fire
The king of Babylon will be overthrown
questions.correctAnswer: The city will be taken and burned with fire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:8 states the LORD's warning that the Chaldeans will come again, fight the city, take it, and burn it with fire.

questions.question: What warning does God give about deceiving yourselves regarding the departure of the Chaldeans?
options: They will be defeated by Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:9 warns not to deceive yourselves by thinking the Chaldeans will depart, for they shall not depart.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 37:10 describe the determination of the Chaldeans even if their army was wounded?
options: They would rise up and burn the city with fire
They would seek peace with Pharaoh
questions.correctAnswer: They would rise up and burn the city with fire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:10 explains that even if the Chaldeans were wounded, they would rise up in their tents and burn Jerusalem with fire.

questions.question: What action did Jeremiah take after the Chaldean army broke up from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army?
options: He went into the land of Benjamin to separate himself
questions.correctAnswer: He went into the land of Benjamin to separate himself
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:12 states Jeremiah went forth out of Jerusalem into the land of Benjamin to separate himself amid the people.

questions.question: What accusation did Irijah, the captain of the ward, make against Jeremiah at the gate of Benjamin?
options: That Jeremiah was conspiring with Pharaoh
That Jeremiah was falling away to the Chaldeans
That Jeremiah had stolen from the temple
questions.correctAnswer: That Jeremiah was falling away to the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:13 records Irijah accusing Jeremiah of falling away to the Chaldeans.

questions.question: How did Jeremiah respond to the accusation made by Irijah?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:14 shows Jeremiah said it was false that he fell away to the Chaldeans, but Irijah did not listen and took him to the princes.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 37 teach us about integrity in the face of false accusations?
options: One should admit guilt to avoid punishment
One should deny false accusations and remain truthful
questions.correctAnswer: One should deny false accusations and remain truthful
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:13-14 show Jeremiah truthfully denied false accusations despite the consequences, teaching integrity and faithfulness in adversity.

questions.question: What practical lesson about trusting God's warnings can be drawn from Jeremiah 37:8-10?
options: Ignore warnings if external help arrives
Trust God's word even if enemies seem to withdraw temporarily
Rely on military alliances over prophecy
Assume peace will come if we pray
questions.correctAnswer: Trust God's word even if enemies seem to withdraw temporarily
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:8-10 warns that despite temporary enemy withdrawal, Jerusalem will be taken and burned, teaching trust in God's warnings over appearances.

questions.question: Based on Jeremiah 37:11-12, what does Jeremiah’s action of separating himself in Benjamin teach about responding to danger and divine instruction?
options: Obey God's guidance even if it means separation from one's people
Join forces with enemies for protection
questions.correctAnswer: Obey God's guidance even if it means separation from one's people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:11-12 shows Jeremiah left Jerusalem and separated himself among the people of Benjamin, indicating obedience to God's direction even when it leads to separation.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 37 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 37.

questions.question: Who was imprisoned in the house of Jonathan the scribe according to Jeremiah 37?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was put in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe by the princes, as stated in Jeremiah 37:15.

questions.question: How did Jeremiah describe his offense to King Zedekiah regarding his imprisonment?
options: He claimed he had offended the king
questions.explanation: Jeremiah told King Zedekiah that he had not offended him or his servants, stating his innocence in Jeremiah 37:18.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah's prophecy to King Zedekiah when asked if there was any word from the LORD?
options: You will be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: You will be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah told King Zedekiah that he would be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon as per Jeremiah 37:17.

questions.question: What did King Zedekiah command regarding Jeremiah's treatment after his initial imprisonment?
options: To commit him into the court of the prison and feed him daily
To put him in the dungeon permanently
questions.correctAnswer: To commit him into the court of the prison and feed him daily
questions.explanation: King Zedekiah ordered Jeremiah to be placed in the prison court and to be given bread daily from the bakers' street as stated in Jeremiah 37:21.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah's concern about returning to the house of Jonathan the scribe?
options: That he would be released too soon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah asked King Zedekiah not to send him back to Jonathan's house, fearing he would die there, as found in Jeremiah 37:20.

questions.question: Who arrested Jeremiah at the gate of Benjamin, accusing him of defecting to the Chaldeans?
questions.explanation: Irijah, the captain of the ward, arrested Jeremiah at the gate of Benjamin, accusing him of defecting, according to Jeremiah 37:13.

questions.question: What caused the Chaldeans to temporarily leave Jerusalem?
options: The arrival of Pharaoh's army from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The arrival of Pharaoh's army from Egypt
questions.explanation: The Chaldeans departed Jerusalem when they heard that Pharaoh's army had come out of Egypt, as described in Jeremiah 37:5.

questions.question: What did the LORD say about relying on Pharaoh's army to save Jerusalem?
options: Pharaoh's army will return to Egypt and Jerusalem will still be taken
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh's army will return to Egypt and Jerusalem will still be taken
questions.explanation: The LORD said Pharaoh's army would return to Egypt and the Chaldeans would come again to take and burn Jerusalem, as in Jeremiah 37:7-8.

questions.question: What literary device is evident when Jeremiah's imprisonment and release contrast with the princes' anger and the king's secret inquiry?
questions.explanation: The chapter uses chiasm by contrasting the princes' anger and Jeremiah's imprisonment with the king's secret questioning and partial mercy, showing a literary mirroring in Jeremiah 37:15-17.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated as 'dungeon' in Jeremiah 37:16?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'dungeon' (מְצוּדָה, metsudah) refers to a dark, confined prison cell, emphasizing Jeremiah's harsh imprisonment in Jeremiah 37:16.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a similar theme of a prophet imprisoned unjustly, as seen with Jeremiah in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Daniel was also unjustly imprisoned for his faithfulness to God, a theme paralleling Jeremiah's imprisonment in Jeremiah 37:15-21 and Daniel 6.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 37 relate to Jesus' experience in the New Testament?
options: Both were imprisoned unjustly for speaking God's truth
questions.correctAnswer: Both were imprisoned unjustly for speaking God's truth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah and Jesus both suffered unjust imprisonment due to their prophetic message, fulfilling a typology of suffering servants (Jeremiah 37:15-21; Matthew 26:57-67).

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was immediately released after King Zedekiah questioned him about God's word.
questions.explanation: Despite King Zedekiah's secret inquiry, Jeremiah was not released but instead confined to the prison court, as shown in Jeremiah 37:21.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah told King Zedekiah that the prophets who said Babylon would not come were correct.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah questioned where those false prophets were who claimed Babylon would not come, indicating their prophecy was incorrect (Jeremiah 37:19).

questions.question: Which historical context best explains why the princes were angry and imprisoned Jeremiah?
options: Jeremiah prophesied Babylon's conquest which was unpopular
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah prophesied Babylon's conquest which was unpopular
questions.explanation: Jeremiah's prophecy of Jerusalem's fall to Babylon angered the princes, causing them to imprison him as per Jeremiah 37:15.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 37 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 37 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Who reigned as king of Judah instead of Coniah?
questions.explanation: Zedekiah, the son of Josiah, reigned instead of Coniah, as stated in Jeremiah 37:1.

questions.question: What did King Zedekiah ask Jeremiah to do?
questions.explanation: Zedekiah sent representatives to Jeremiah asking him to pray unto the LORD for them, as stated in Jeremiah 37:3.

questions.question: What was the fate of Jerusalem according to the word of the LORD?
questions.explanation: The LORD declared that the Chaldeans would come again, fight against the city, and burn it with fire, as stated in Jeremiah 37:8.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah say about the Chaldeans' departure?
options: They will come back to fight
questions.correctAnswer: They will come back to fight
questions.explanation: Jeremiah warned that the Chaldeans shall not depart and will come again to fight against the city, as stated in Jeremiah 37:9.

questions.question: What accusation was made against Jeremiah by Irijah?
options: He was fleeing to the Chaldeans
questions.correctAnswer: He was fleeing to the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: Irijah accused Jeremiah, saying he was falling away to the Chaldeans, as stated in Jeremiah 37:13.

questions.question: What was Zedekiah's secret inquiry to Jeremiah?
options: What shall I do to save Jerusalem?
Is there any word from the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Is there any word from the LORD?
questions.explanation: Zedekiah secretly asked Jeremiah if there was any word from the LORD, as stated in Jeremiah 37:17.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah's response to Zedekiah's inquiry?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah told Zedekiah that he would be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, as stated in Jeremiah 37:17.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah plead with the king regarding his imprisonment?
options: To not return to Jonathan's house
To be given a better cell
To be allowed to speak to his followers
questions.correctAnswer: To not return to Jonathan's house
questions.explanation: Jeremiah pleaded with Zedekiah to not send him back to the house of Jonathan, lest he die there, as stated in Jeremiah 37:20.

questions.question: What was the condition of Jeremiah while in prison?
questions.explanation: Zedekiah commanded that Jeremiah should be given daily a piece of bread until the bread in the city was spent, as stated in Jeremiah 37:21.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah's experience in prison reveal about human opposition to God's prophets?
options: They often reject and punish them
questions.correctAnswer: They often reject and punish them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was smitten and put in prison for his prophecies, showing the common human tendency to oppose God's messengers, as indicated in Jeremiah 37:15.

questions.question: What theological concept does Jeremiah's imprisonment highlight?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah’s imprisonment and the prophecies of coming judgment illustrate God's sovereignty over nations and events, as the prophecies come to pass regardless of human actions.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Jeremiah 37:6 where He communicates with His prophet?
questions.explanation: The act of God speaking to Jeremiah shows His attribute of revelation, as God communicates His will and plans to His prophet, as stated in Jeremiah 37:6.

questions.question: What does the interaction between Zedekiah and Jeremiah reveal about the nature of authority?
questions.explanation: Zedekiah sought Jeremiah's counsel yet imprisoned him for his prophecies, indicating a conflicted nature of authority that does not align with divine guidance.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that God does not speak to His people today. What does Jeremiah 37:6-7 teach?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 37:6-7 shows that God spoke to Jeremiah, indicating that God continues to actively communicate His will and guidance to His people.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah's prophecy about Babylon's conquest fit into the larger narrative of Scripture?
options: It illustrates the power of man
questions.explanation: Jeremiah's prophecy about Babylon's conquest of Jerusalem demonstrates God's judgment on His people for their disobedience, fitting into the broader narrative of God's holiness and justice throughout Scripture.
